SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
REPORT
（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE S. BR. REGISTRY No N. 1502(C) Date 7/4/42）
Special Branch Station. File No. Date March 31, 1942

SUBJECT: Sub-Inspector S.G. Nadeyeff - Letter to Editor of "New Times".

With reference to the endorsement of the Officer i/c Special Branch on the attached translation from the "New Times" of 23-3-42, enquiries have been made regarding the circumstances which led to the appearance of Sub-Inspector S.G. Nadeyeff's letter to the Editor of the "New Times".

It would appear that rumours to the effect that he is a member of the local Soviet Citizens Club are based on a list of members of that club compiled some time in July, 1941 by an individual who is reported to have been engaged in anti-Soviet intelligence work for the past several years. A copy of this list has been obtained from a confidential source in connection with the present enquiries. In it is mentioned under No.199 one "N.Nadeyeff". It will be seen that the initial of this individual does not correspond to those of Sub-Inspector Nadeyeff ( S.G. ). Several other inaccuracies have been noticed in the list in question which, together with the obscure origin of this document, suggest that information it contains must be accepted with extreme caution and reserve.

Interviewed by the undersigned on 28-3-42 Sub-Inspector Nadeyeff confirmed that on 30-10-41, being annoyed by the persistent rumours referred to above, he addressed a letter to the Chairman of the Russian Emigrants Committee requesting him to cause enquiries to be made regarding the origin of the rumours and persons spreading them in order that his good name as a Russian

主题：副督察 S.G. Nadeyeff —— 致《新时报》编辑的信。

鉴于特别分部主管警官对附上的1942年3月23日《新时报》译文所作的批注，已就导致副督察 S.G. Nadeyeff 致信《新时报》编辑一事的相关情况进行了调查。

看来，有关他是当地苏联公民俱乐部成员的谣言，是基于该俱乐部的一份成员名单，该名单据称由一名在过去几年中从事反苏情报工作的人士于1941年7月某时编制。作为本次调查的一部分，已从机密来源获取了该名单的副本。其中第199号列有一名“N.Nadeyeff”。可以看出，此人的名字首字母与副督察 Nadeyeff (S.G.) 的首字母不符。在该名单中还发现了其他几处不准确之处，加之该文件来源不明，表明必须极其谨慎和保留地接受其中包含的信息。

副督察 Nadeyeff 于1942年3月28日接受下文签署人问询时证实，1941年10月30日，因受上述持续谣言的困扰，他致信俄罗斯侨民委员会主席，请求其调查谣言的来源及散布者，以便保护他作为一名俄罗斯

Sub-Inspector Nadeyeff's antecedents and ge-
neral reputation in the Russian community do not in the
least suggest that he is a Soviet sympathiser, and it
has been ascertained that the Russian Emigrants Commit-
tee does not give any credence to the above allegation
against him. Moreover, it is quite possible that the
said rumours originated through a/ misunderstanding. In
this connection it is of interest to note that on
9-3-42 died in Shanghai one N.I. Nadeyenko, a musician,
who registered with the Russian Emigrants Committee in
1932. Following his death , the Russian Emigrants Com-
mittee was informed by the French Police that amongst
the belongings of the deceased his Soviet passport had
been found. It is very likely that he was a member of
the Soviet Citizens Club and that his name was confused
with that of Sub-Inspector S.G. Nadeyeff.

When addressing his letter to the Chairman of

主题：
侨民的名誉。

副督察 Nadeyeff 的履历及其在俄罗斯社区中的一般声誉，丝毫不能表明他是苏联的同情者；且经查实，俄罗斯侨民委员会并不相信上述对他的指控。此外，这些谣言很可能源于误会。在此方面，值得注意的是，1942年3月9日，音乐家 N.I. Nadeyenko 在上海去世，他于1932年在俄罗斯侨民委员会注册。在他去世后，法国警察通知俄罗斯侨民委员会，在死者的遗物中发现了他的苏联护照。他很有可能是苏联公民俱乐部的成员，其名字与副督察 S.G. Nadeyeff 的名字发生了混淆。

去年十月致信俄罗斯侨民委员会主席时，副督察 Nadeyeff 表示，身为警察，他无法在报刊上维护自己的名誉。令人遗憾的是，他对此事的态度发生了转变，并在静安寺警署协理主管 Sugisaki 首席督察的许可下，向《新时报》编辑发出了附件中的信件。鉴于1941年12月28日他成为俄罗斯周报《NASH POOT》（见档案

D.8149 - F.136 ). Hereunder is a translation of an ex-
tract from the article in questions:-

"... It is an open secret ,for instance,that
contributions towards the British War Fund played an im-
portant part in the matter of promotion of Russian mem-
bers of the S.M.Police. Certain individuals,who were
particularly interested in promotion,contributed consi-
derable amounts regularly every month and were not dis-
sappointed in their expectations: they were noticed,re-
garded as being nice fellows and usually were selected
for promotion".

"One of such ambitious persons,who at one time
contributed money towards the British War Fund under the
pseudonym "MOLOTOV",went so far in his yearning for pro-
motion to the rank of Sub-Inspector that he sent his
daughters to a children's party attended by many of his
British chiefs,wearing broad ribbons over their shoul-
ders with the words "GOD SAVE ENGLAND" printed on them
in bold type!"

"This contemptible lackey got what he desired:
he was promoted over the heads of his Russian colleagues,
including many men of meritorious service,intelligence
and Honour."

According to Sub-Inspector Nadeyeff,the true
facts about the above outburst are as follows:-

1. Some time in 1939,following the conclusion
of the Soviet-German Non-Aggression Pact,when the name
of V.Molotov,Soviet Commissar for Foreign Affairs, was
frequently mentioned in the press and conversations,one
of Nadeyeff's colleagues at Bubbling Well Station nick-
named him "Molotov" by way of a joke.

2.In December,1939 and February,1940 he sub-
scribed $10.00 on each occasion towards the British War
Comfort Fund under his own name. He believes that lists
of subscribers were published in the "North China Daily
News". Subscriptions lists were available at each Po-
lice Station.

3.Some time about Christmas in 1939/40 or
1940/41 his daughters attended a Fancy Dress Party for
children at the home of Sergeant R.S. Winsett. One of
them wore a costume which had been given to her by an
English lady friend who was leaving for Canada. The de-
tails of the costume included the British national flag,
the inscriptions "Britannia" and "Buy British goods" dis-
played on the chest,head-dress and belt,respectively.

The rest of the story ,Sub-Inspector Nadeyeff
stated, were invented by the gentlemen from the "Nash
Post".

Officer i/c Special Branch                  A. Prokazin
                                            D.I.

D.8149 - F.136），这一行动在某种程度上是可以理解的。以下是有关文章摘录的译文：-

“……例如，这是一个公开的秘密，向英国战争基金捐款在公共租界警务处俄罗斯籍成员的晋升事宜中发挥了重要作用。某些特别渴望晋升的人每月定期捐赠巨额款项，并且没有失望：他们受到关注，被视为好人，通常被选中晋升”。

“其中一位野心勃勃的人，曾以‘莫洛托夫’为化名向英国战争基金捐款，他对晋升副督察一职的渴望如此强烈，以至于让他的女儿们参加有许多英国上司出席的儿童派对时，肩上佩戴着印有粗体字‘上帝保佑英格兰’的宽丝带！”

“这个卑鄙的奴才得到了他想要的东西：他越过他的俄罗斯同事，包括许多有功绩、有才智和荣誉的人，获得了晋升。”

据副督察 Nadeyeff 称，上述抨击的真实情况如下：-

1. 1939年某时，在苏德互不侵犯条约签订后，当苏联外交人民委员 V. Molotov 的名字经常在报刊和谈话中被提及之时，静安寺警署的一位同事开玩笑地给他起了个绰号叫“莫洛托夫”。

2. 1939年12月和1940年2月，他以自己的名义两次向英国战争慰劳基金各捐款10.00美元。他认为捐款人名单刊登在《字林西报》上。各警署均可查阅捐款人名单。

3. 1939/40年或1940/41年圣诞节前后，他的女儿们参加了 R.S. Winsett 巡长家中举办的儿童化装舞会。其中一人穿着一套由一位即将前往加拿大的英国女性友人赠送的服装。这套服装的细节包括英国国旗，以及分别显示在胸前、头饰和腰带上的铭文“不列颠尼亚”和“购买英国货”。

副督察 Nadeyeff 表示，故事的其余部分均由《Nash Post》的那些先生们捏造。

特别分部主管警官                  A. Prokazin

Translation from Russian.

THE NEW TIMES MARCH 23, 1942

Letter to the Editor.

Sir,
Will you be good enough to publish the
following in your esteemed journal:-
Approximately in the end of August, 1941 I became
aware of rumours alleging that I am a member of the local
Soviet Citizens' Club and that I am contributing towards the
Red Army Fund under the pseudonym "Molotov".
I immediately applied to Colonel N.K. Serejnikoff,
Head of the Russian Emigrant Community, with a request to ren-
der me assistance in the matter of refuting this malicious
calumny.
Colonel Serejnikoff advised me to make a state-
ment in writing on this subject addressed to him, consider-
ing that this would be quite sufficient for my rehabilitation.
I acted accordingly.
It has come to my knowledge at present that the
same rumour is again current and therefore I deem it neces-
sary to publish the above for general information.

I am, etc.

(Signed:) S.G. NADEYEFF

S. 3.
Eng & report
the circumstances.
（批：JM）

Translator's note: The writer of the above letter is
Sub-Inspector S.G. Nadeyeff, Shanghai
Municipal Police.

March 23, 1942.

A. Prokofiev
D.I.

俄文译文。

《新时报》 1942年3月23日

致编辑的信。

先生，
能否请您在贵刊上发表以下内容：-
大约在1941年8月底，我得知有谣言称我是当地苏联公民俱乐部的成员，并且我以“莫洛托夫”为化名向红军基金捐款。
我立即向俄罗斯侨民社区负责人 N.K. Serejnikoff 上校提出申请，请求他协助我驳斥这一恶意的诽谤。
Serejnikoff 上校建议我就此事向他提交一份书面声明，认为这足以恢复我的名誉。
我照办了。
目前我获悉，同样的谣言再次流传，因此我认为有必要公布上述内容，以广周知。

此致，

（签名：） S.G. NADEYEFF

S. 3.
英文及报告
相关情况。
（批注：JM）
